Timeline/1949
1949Research monograph

Memory & learning

Learning leaves a lasting neural trace

Cell assemblies and activity-dependent changes connected learning with the organization of neural circuits.

Donald O. Hebb

AI topics

Explore related entries. Larger tags appear on more entries.

MemoryNeural networksAssociative memoryLearning theory

The contribution

Hebb proposed that repeated coordinated activity could strengthen connections between neurons, allowing groups of cells to act together as assemblies. The theory connected lasting changes in connections with perception, learning, and memory. It supplied a biological hypothesis that later neural models could formalize as rules for storing associations.

What this does not establish

This is a theory of neural organization, not a tested general-purpose AI architecture. The familiar slogan about neurons firing together compresses a more specific proposal.

Why this date?

1949 dates the original Wiley edition. Later reprints and digital copies retain the original work but have different publication dates.
